# UX and Accessibility Requirements Quality Checklist: Projects — creation, record, membership and lifecycle

**Purpose**: Validate that the interaction, state, ordering and accessibility requirements for Create project, Project details and the shell regions are complete, unambiguous, consistent and objectively verifiable before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-08-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## In-Place Editing

- [x] CHK001 Is the in-place edit affordance specified for input other than a click, given FR-036 names clicking the value as the only way to open a field? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-036]
- [x] CHK002 Is a non-macOS equivalent specified for the ⌘-enter save shortcut? [Gap, Spec §FR-036]
- [x] CHK003 Are focus-management requirements stated for what receives focus when a field opens, saves, reverts on Escape, or rolls back? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-036, §FR-038]
- [x] CHK004 Is it specified whether more than one field may be open for editing at once, and what a blur that opens a second field does to the first? [Gap, Spec §FR-036]
- [x] CHK005 Are requirements stated for a second in-place save begun while the first is still in flight? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §FR-036, §FR-038]
- [x] CHK006 Is it specified whether a blur with an unchanged value issues an `updateProject` call, given FR-036 requires exactly one call per field? [Clarity, Spec §FR-036]
- [x] CHK007 Is the surface for the rollback message specified — inline on the field, a transient notification, or both? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-038, §FR-041]

## Optimistic and Pending State

- [x] CHK008 Is the criterion that decides which writes are optimistic stated as a rule, or only as an enumeration that leaves a new write unclassified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-033, §FR-038, §FR-041, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK009 Is the roster add and remove write's optimistic behaviour stated as a requirement, rather than appearing only under Assumptions? [Traceability, Spec §FR-045, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK010 Are pending and skeleton-state requirements stated for the two screens this feature adds, or explicitly delegated to a named inherited convention? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK011 Are screen-reader announcement requirements stated for an optimistic write that later reverts, so the reversion is perceivable without sight of the value? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-038, §FR-041]
- [x] CHK012 Are requirements stated for a server error that prevents the details screen from loading at all, as distinct from a refused write? [Gap, Exception Flow, Spec §FR-035, §FR-040]

## Create Project Form

- [x] CHK013 Is "word" defined for key derivation — how hyphens, apostrophes, digits and repeated separators are treated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK014 Are validation-timing requirements consistent between FR-032's per-field-on-blur rule and FR-026's submit-time re-check? [Consistency, Spec §FR-026, §FR-032]
- [x] CHK015 Are timing or debounce requirements stated for the as-typed key check? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-026]
- [x] CHK016 Are requirements stated for how a user learns a field's length bound before exceeding it? [Gap, Spec §FR-012, §FR-024, §FR-027]
- [x] CHK017 Is "grow with its content" bounded — is a maximum height or scroll behaviour specified? [Clarity, Measurability, Spec §FR-027]
- [x] CHK018 Is Cancel's destination specified when the user arrived at `/projects/new` directly rather than from another screen? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK019 Is the palette swatch control's accessible naming specified, so a swatch can be identified and chosen without perceiving its colour? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-029]

## Details Screen, Status and Delete

- [x] CHK020 Does FR-021's disabled-control-with-reason rule apply to the Columns section, where FR-044 states no control exists at all? [Consistency, Spec §FR-021, §FR-044]
- [x] CHK021 Is an empty-state requirement stated for a project whose roster holds no members, given FR-045 permits removing the last one? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-045, §FR-055]
- [x] CHK022 Can FR-048's "states the size of what it will destroy" be objectively verified without a specified format for the statement? [Measurability, Spec §FR-048]
- [x] CHK023 Is the destination after a successful delete specified, or only that the browser navigates away? [Gap, Spec §FR-052]
- [x] CHK024 Are requirements stated for how the confirmation is dismissed and what happens to the screen when it is declined? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §FR-048]

## Ordering, Shell and Presentation

- [x] CHK025 Is the collation for the sidebar's alphabetical order specified for non-ASCII and locale-varying names? [Clarity, Spec §FR-053]
- [x] CHK026 Is a deterministic tiebreaker specified for two projects with identical names, given SC-013 requires every user to see the same order? [Gap, Consistency, Spec §FR-053, §SC-013, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK027 Is a non-colour indicator required alongside the palette colour dot and the archived "dimmed" treatment, so neither state is conveyed by colour alone? [Gap, Accessibility, Spec §FR-053, §FR-054, §FR-056]
- [x] CHK028 Are truncation or overflow requirements stated for long project names in the sidebar and the screen header? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §FR-053, §FR-056]
- [x] CHK029 Are viewport, responsive or text-direction requirements stated for the two screens, or explicitly delegated to a named inherited convention? [Gap, Non-Functional, Spec §FR-022, §FR-035]

## Success Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK030 Are the measurement conditions for SC-001's two-minute target stated — which actor, which starting point and which network assumptions? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [x] CHK031 Is SC-006's "visible within one interaction" quantified, or does it restate the optimistic rule without adding a measurable threshold? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, §FR-038]
- [x] CHK032 Is there a measurable success criterion covering the accessibility obligations the functional requirements imply, or does the criteria set omit that dimension entirely? [Gap, Coverage, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Resolution log

Recorded 2026-08-31 at the reviewer's request, after walking every item against
[`docs/product/specifications.md`](../../../docs/product/specifications.md),
[`docs/product/requirements-index.md`](../../../docs/product/requirements-index.md),
[`AGENTS.md`](../../../AGENTS.md) and this feature's own plan artifacts.

**Covered** — the requirement was already answered, in this spec or in a document it inherits from; the
citation is given and nothing changed. **Resolved** — the gap was real and a change was made; what
changed is named.

- **CHK001** · *Resolved* — FR-036: the editable value is a control, not static text — it carries an accessible name, a visible focus indicator and keyboard activation, and must not be reachable by pointer alone.
- **CHK002** · *Resolved* — FR-036: Ctrl-enter saves on a platform with no ⌘ key.
- **CHK003** · *Resolved* — FR-036: focus returns to the control when the field closes, whether it saved or reverted. Everything below that is §7's delegation to React Aria.
- **CHK004** · *Resolved* — FR-036: at most one field open at a time — opening a second closes the first through the blur that FR-036 already makes a save.
- **CHK005** · *Covered* — §4's *Slow write* row: "The control shows in-flight state and stays interactive-blocked only for itself." Per-control, so a second field is never blocked by the first.
- **CHK006** · *Resolved* — FR-036: a blur whose value is unchanged makes no call at all.
- **CHK007** · *Covered* — §4's *Rejected write* row: "The change rolls back and a toast names what failed and why." §3.4, §3.8 and §3.12 all name the toast.
- **CHK008** · *Covered* — §4's *Slow write* row states a criterion, not an enumeration: "Small, local writes … apply immediately and roll back on failure; anything larger waits for the server." `OT-UX-008` restates it.
- **CHK009** · *Covered* — A roster toggle is one row from one control, which the §4 criterion classes as small and local. The *Assumptions* entry reasons to exactly that — the right home for an application of a stated rule.
- **CHK010** · *Covered* — §4's *Loading* row: "Per-screen skeletons that match the layout they replace… never a layout shift when data lands."
- **CHK011** · *Covered* — §7 delegates ARIA semantics to React Aria Components, whose Toast is a live region, and AGENTS.md repeats the obligation. Availability in the pinned version is a plan concern, and research records it.
- **CHK012** · *Resolved* — Added to *Inherited constraints*: the connection-lost banner, the failed-load treatment and the toast conventions are entry R2's cross-cutting states (§4), not this feature's to define.
- **CHK013** · *Resolved* — FR-025: the first character of each whitespace-separated word, with no other separator splitting a word — `Re-Design` derives `R`. Both of §3.7's worked examples still hold.
- **CHK014** · *Covered* — No conflict — §3.7 states both. Per-field on blur is about presentation ("never a wall of errors on submit"); the submit re-check is about the race the as-typed check cannot win.
- **CHK015** · *Resolved* — Recorded as a default: how often the field asks is a matter for the screen, not for the requirements document.
- **CHK016** · *Resolved* — Recorded as a default: a bounded field refuses input past its bound rather than accepting it and rejecting it afterwards, which is the option that never produces an error the user could not see coming.
- **CHK017** · *Resolved* — FR-027: grows with its content up to a maximum height, then scrolls within itself.
- **CHK018** · *Resolved* — FR-034: Home, where the user arrived at the route directly and there is nowhere to return to.
- **CHK019** · *Covered* — AGENTS.md: "Every control needs an accessible name." §7's palette names the seven colours, which is what supplies it.
- **CHK020** · *Covered* — No conflict — §3.8: "For everyone else this is a read-only list of the board's columns and their counts." §2's rule governs actions a user cannot take; where the feature offers the action to nobody, there is no control to disable.
- **CHK021** · *Covered* — §4's *Empty* row: "One quiet line per surface. No illustrations, no empty-state marketing."
- **CHK022** · *Covered* — §3.10 gives the canonical form for a cascade confirmation — "Delete *blocked*? It will be removed from 14 issues. This can't be undone." — and §3.8 requires the size stated on the same terms.
- **CHK023** · *Resolved* — FR-052: Home, being the one destination that still resolves once the project is gone.
- **CHK024** · *Covered* — §3.9 and §3.10 fix the modal convention — "Cancel or Escape closes it and discards" — and §7 delegates the dialog behaviour to React Aria.
- **CHK025** · *Resolved* — FR-053: the name comparison is case-insensitive, which is what US5 scenario 1 was already asserting.
- **CHK026** · *Resolved* — FR-053: the project's key breaks the tie, being unique and immutable, so the order is total and SC-013 is satisfiable rather than merely stated.
- **CHK027** · *Covered* — AGENTS.md: "Never convey state or errors through colour alone." Archived is additionally carried by position — FR-053 sorts every active project before every archived one.
- **CHK028** · *Resolved* — FR-054 and FR-056: visually truncated with the whole name still available to assistive technology, never wrapped, never widening the sidebar region and never displacing the header's tabs.
- **CHK029** · *Covered* — §1: "Desktop-only: v1 targets a desktop browser", with responsive and mobile layouts explicitly out of scope; §3's shell adds "No mobile breakpoint."
- **CHK030** · *Covered* — SC-001 already names the actor (an admin), the starting point (an empty installation) and the path (a name plus every default). For a two-minute human-task budget, hardware and network are noise.
- **CHK031** · *Covered* — "Within one interaction" is the optimistic rule's observable — the value changes on the gesture rather than after a round trip — and SC-006 adds "with no page reload in either case". Verifiable as written.
- **CHK032** · *Resolved* — SC-018 added: every in-place value can be opened, changed, saved and reverted by keyboard alone, with focus visible at each step and never lost to the document body.

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
